note: heal-check under Git Bash's perl, from a skill's helper whose parent chain is the Bash tool's shells (STORE_TEST_PPID 885, STORE_TEST_PROC: 885 -> 841 -> 1, no Claude Code above): the walk takes CLAUDE_PID (identity::_walk), so the identity is the session's record and the relation same-session or successor, never degraded. The owner of a job with no job record is its origin's newest live record, judged by skills::ctx::pid_state through identity::liveness (seams as WIN-ID-01, at +03). (1) This session in the Git Bash shape (CLAUDE_PID 12044 maps to a running MSYS pid with the recorded start): owner 'this', the job RUNNING, never relaunched. (2) A predecessor whose record names a pid only `ps -W` lists (alive-unknown, start null): owner unverified, V2 unmeasured, NOT-LOST, never LOST or ok. (3) A /clear predecessor whose start is recorded and whose pid is alive-unknown (jobs::_cleared): V2 unmeasured, never LOST. (4a) The same predecessor with no `ps -W` listing (a missing file): a pid that nothing maps is unknown, never gone: NOT-LOST. (4b) A newer record of it whose start is recorded and whose pid only `ps -W` lists (alive-unknown, owner_state through pid_state): NOT-LOST. (4) Control: once its pids neither map nor are listed they are gone: LOST, high, ok, as on Unix. (5) The PowerShell shape (CLAUDE_PID 22192, no MSYS pid, start unknown): the session's own record (start null on both sides) is found, same-session, owner unverified: NOT-LOST, never LOST
